title: Brands in numbers
heading: How far off is your gut?
intro: Eight real facts and figures about brands: what they are worth, where their names and symbols come from, and who buys them where.
Every figure is real and sourced. Bet on how sure you are.

outro.heading: A brand lives in other people's heads.
paras: Fake branded goods are worth hundreds of billions in world trade; some of the best-known names began as a founder's initials or a family quarrel; and the country that buys the most bottles of a famous product isn't always the one you'd expect.
Brands are often worth more, and known less well, than we assume.

questions.q: The German sweet brand Haribo, maker of the gold bears, takes its name from...
options: its founder's name and home town
questions.explain: Hans Riegel founded the company in Bonn in 1920 and built its name from the first two letters of each: HAns RIegel BOnn. His first gummy bear, the 'Dancing Bear', followed in 1922; the Goldbears name arrived in 1960.

questions.q: Adidas and Puma were both founded by two brothers, Adi and Rudolf Dassler, who fell out and split their shoe company. In which town are both still based?
questions.explain: The Dassler brothers split their company in 1948. Rudolf founded Puma that year, and in 1949 Adi named his own firm after himself: adidas, from ADI DASsler. Both companies still have their headquarters in the same small town near Nuremberg.

questions.q: Louis Vuitton's parent group, LVMH, is the world's largest luxury company. How many separate brands ('Maisons') does it own?
questions.explain: LVMH counts 75 Maisons, among them Louis Vuitton, Dior, Moët & Chandon, Hennessy, Sephora and Tiffany. Together they had revenue of €80.8 billion in 2025, with more than 211,000 employees and about 6,300 shops.
questions.source: LVMH, Letter to shareholders, January 2026 (2025 key figures)

questions.q: Brand Finance values the world's brands every year. In its 2026 ranking, which is Germany's most valuable brand?
questions.explain: Deutsche Telekom's brand was valued at US$96.2 billion, a record, and it was the only European brand in the global top 20. Mercedes-Benz came 36th and BMW 41st, and SAP entered the top 50 for the first time. Many people guess a car maker.

questions.q: Scotland exported about 1.3 billion bottles of Scotch whisky in 2025: around 43 every second. Which country bought the most bottles?
questions.explain: India bought 220 million bottles, ahead of France (152m) and the United States (120m); Germany was fourth (59m). By value, though, the US is still the biggest market (£933m), because it buys more expensive whisky.
questions.source: Scotch Whisky Association, 2025 export figures (HMRC data)

questions.q: The OECD and the EU's intellectual property office estimate how much of world trade is in fake branded goods. What share of all world imports is counterfeit?
questions.explain: Counterfeit goods made up an estimated 2.3% of world imports, worth about US$467 billion, in 2021, the latest year studied. Clothing, footwear and leather goods made up about 62% of seizures. The figure is an estimate based on customs seizure data.
questions.source: OECD and EUIPO, Mapping Global Trade in Fakes 2025

questions.q: The Austrian energy-drink company Red Bull publishes its sales every year. How many cans did it sell worldwide in 2025?
questions.explain: Red Bull sold 13.969 billion cans in 2025, up about 10% on 2024: more than one and a half for every person on Earth. Turnover rose to about €12.2 billion. The company also runs two Formula 1 teams.

questions.q: Daimler applied to protect the Mercedes-Benz three-pointed star as a trademark in 1909. What do its three points stand for?
options: Engines for land, sea and air
questions.explain: The star stands for Daimler's aim to build engines for use on land, at sea and in the air. It goes back to a star Gottlieb Daimler drew on an 1872 postcard to mark his home; his sons later turned it into the company's trademark.
questions.source: Mercedes-Benz Group brand history, as reported by Motor1
